item_title: Borderless.xyz, Mastercard pilot stablecoin trust tool
item_text:
News
Crypto, Web3 and CBDC
Borderless.xyz and Mastercard pilot stablecoin trust framework
Sinziana Albu
06 Aug 2026 / 5 Min Read
Borderless.xyz and Mastercard have launched a pilot to explore trust standards for cross-border stablecoin payments.
Stablecoins are increasingly used to move value across borders, offering participants faster and more efficient payment options. In addition, as adoption expands, the companies said, participants need reliable ways to confirm counterparties' identities and verify that they meet applicable standards and requirements.
The pilot will examine how Mastercard Crypto Credential can address this by generating assurance signals that participants can fold into their own approval, compliance, and risk management processes. Mastercard Crypto Credential is designed to support verifiable interactions across digital asset ecosystems by applying common standards intended to add confidence, transparency, and certainty to transactions conducted across blockchain networks.
According to
Kevin Lehtiniitty
, CEO and co-founder of Borderless.xyz, one recurring friction point for stablecoin payment operators is that compliance processes do not scale at the same pace as the payment network itself, since each new provider currently requires the verification process to be repeated. In addition, he compared the approach being piloted to the model used in correspondent banking, where originating compliance is trusted by downstream parties rather than re-executed at every counterparty, noting that Mastercard is applying a similar logic to digital asset payments through the Borderless.xyz network.
Raj Dhamodharan
, executive vice president for blockchain and digital assets at Mastercard, said the collaboration builds on a relationship that began through Start Path, Mastercard's startup engagement programme, and has developed as the digital asset ecosystem has matured.
Network participants and scope
The pilot combines Mastercard's work on trust standards for digital asset ecosystems with Borderless.xyz's network of stablecoin payment providers. Through the collaboration, the companies aim to determine how trusted governance signals can reduce friction and increase confidence in cross-border stablecoin payments as adoption increases.
Several participants in the Borderless.xyz network are involved in the pilot, including Infinia, Walapay, and Koywe, a number of which are also alumni of Mastercard Start Path. Under the pilot, these operators are among the first stablecoin payment providers to run on what the companies describe as a single-audit compliance model applied at network scale, meaning that a single compliance verification could be recognised across multiple network participants rather than assessed individually by each one.
Mastercard has been developing Crypto Credential as part of its broader digital asset infrastructure work, aimed at giving participants in blockchain-based payment networks a consistent way to verify counterparties. The Borderless.xyz pilot represents an application of that framework specifically to cross-border stablecoin payment flows, an area where regulatory and compliance requirements can vary by jurisdiction and counterparty.

item_title: 10x Banking raises GBP 40 million from AshGrove Capital
item_text:
News
Fintech
10x Banking secures GBP 40 million from AshGrove Capital
Sinziana Albu
06 Aug 2026 / 5 Min Read
10x Banking has raised GBP 40 million from AshGrove Capital, following a year of profitability, account growth, and expanded revenue.
The investment follows a period in which 10x Banking became EBITDA-positive while continuing to grow its client base and revenue.
Per the official press release, over the past twelve months, 10x Banking reported that it became EBITDA-positive, surpassed ten million live accounts, and onboarded more than ten new financial institutions. The company also stated that its annual recurring revenue (ARR) increased by over 30% during the same period.
According to 10x Banking, these figures reflect demand from financial institutions looking to replace legacy infrastructure that was not designed for real-time processing, continuous product development, or the data requirements associated with AI-enabled banking services.
Antony Jenkins, founder, chair, and chief executive officer of 10x Banking, said financial institutions face constraints from infrastructure that was not built for real-time, digital banking, and that the company was created to address this gap. He added that the AshGrove investment supports the company's ability to meet demand from banks internationally.
Use of proceeds and strategic context
The funding is intended to support the continued expansion of 10x Banking's sales and go-to-market capabilities. AshGrove Capital becomes a new investor in the company, joining what 10x Banking describes as a client base that has continued to extend its use of the platform.
Phil Fretwell
, co-founder and managing partner of AshGrove Capital, said the firm's decision reflects confidence in 10x Banking's revenue growth, cost management, and technical execution at scale, noting that delivering a cloud-native banking platform across large volumes of live accounts represents a significant operational undertaking.
Nadir Guessoum
, chief financial officer of 10x Banking, said the AshGrove investment strengthens the company's balance sheet and supports its growth strategy, and that reaching EBITDA profitability alongside continued ARR growth reflects the commercial progress made to date.
The transaction takes place against a backdrop in which banks across multiple regions are reassessing legacy core banking infrastructure. Financial institutions are increasingly citing requirements for real-time processing, faster product deployment, and data architectures capable of supporting AI-based banking applications as reasons to modernise underlying systems. 10x Banking's position as a fourth-generation core banking platform provider, working with institutions such as Westpac and Chase UK, places the funding within this broader pattern of infrastructure renewal across the banking sector.

item_title: Wero delays Luxembourg launch to 1 September 2026
item_text:
News
Payments
Wero delays Luxembourg launch to 1 September
Sinziana Albu
06 Aug 2026 / 5 Min Read
The European Payments Initiative has pushed back Wero's official launch in Luxembourg from June to 1 September 2026.
Acourding to Luxembourg Times, BGL BNP Paribas, BIL, Raiffeisen, and Spuerkeess had jointly stated in March 2026 that they would be ready to offer Wero to their respective clients by the end of June 2026, with Post Luxembourg expected to follow by mid-August 2026 at the earliest. As of the original June deadline, none of the participating banks had launched the app, and the institutions did not respond to requests for comment.
EPI has now set 1 September 2026 as the official market launch date for Luxembourg. The organisation said the timing was chosen to avoid the summer holiday period, when media attention, customer engagement, and market visibility tend to decline. In addition, EPI noted that launching a new payment brand depends on more than technical readiness, requiring coordinated communications and customer awareness alongside system preparation. Individual banks may continue to follow their own deployment schedules, meaning some could launch before September while others align with the official date.
Payconiq wind-down
The revised timeline comes ahead of the scheduled closure of Payconiq, the mobile payment app Wero is intended to replace in Luxembourg. Payconiq will be permanently withdrawn from the market from 30 September 2026, requiring users to register with Wero before that date to maintain uninterrupted access to mobile payments. During the transition, both services will run in parallel, allowing customers to continue using Payconiq while setting up Wero accounts. Merchants have until the end of September 2026 to replace existing Payconiq QR codes with Wero-branded alternatives.
Wero's European rollout
Wero is a pan-European digital wallet developed by EPI, a consortium of major European banks established to build a domestic instant-payment alternative to international card networks such as Visa and Mastercard. The service enables instant account-to-account transfers using a phone number or email address, QR code payments, invoice settlement, and online purchases made directly from a bank account. Wero is already operational in Germany, France, and Belgium, with Luxembourg forming part of its continued expansion across the region. The delay illustrates the operational coordination required across multiple national banking systems as EPI works towards broader adoption of a shared European payment infrastructure.

item_title: norisbank adds Wero payment app for customers
item_text:
News
Payments
norisbank introduces Wero payment app for customers
Sinziana Albu
06 Aug 2026 / 5 Min Read
norisbank has introduced the Wero payment app, enabling customers to send money and pay online across Europe.
The app removes the need to enter an IBAN or BIC, allowing transactions to be completed in a way comparable to sending a text message from a smartphone.
Wero is linked directly to a customer's norisbank current account, with amounts debited or credited immediately and no requirement for prior top-up. norisbank stated that the integration is intended to simplify cross-border banking for its customers as a direct bank. According to Maik Wennrich, chairman of the management board of norisbank GmbH, the rollout follows earlier launches at Deutsche Bank and Postbank and is positioned as a European alternative aimed at combining security, efficiency, and digital sovereignty. The company added that Wero will be integrated into the norisbank app itself in future, with the aim of further simplifying digital payments for its customer base.
Background on Wero and EPI
Wero was launched in July 2024 and is operated by the European Payments Initiative (EPI), an alliance backed by 18 major European banks and payment service providers. The initiative's stated aim is to establish a unified mobile payment solution and a digital wallet for use across Europe, positioning Wero as an alternative to non-European payment schemes for both peer-to-peer transfers and retail transactions.
Since autumn 2025, Wero has supported payments for goods and services at participating online merchants, extending its functionality beyond person-to-person transfers. EPI has outlined further plans for the service, including support for recurring payments such as subscriptions and point-of-sale payments at physical retail locations. Additional features under development include ‘buy now, pay later’ functionality, integration with merchant loyalty programmes, and tools for managing shared expenses among users.
Martina Weimert, chief executive officer of the European Payments Initiative, said the addition of norisbank extends the scheme's network of participating banks, with the stated goal of offering a single, secure payment method for individuals and businesses across national borders in Europe. The rollout at norisbank follows the same pattern seen at Deutsche Bank and Postbank, indicating a phased expansion of Wero across banking groups operating in the German market.
For norisbank, the addition of Wero is framed as part of a broader effort to strengthen its digital current account offering, alongside existing services such as overnight money products. The bank did not disclose a specific timeline for the planned integration of Wero directly into its own mobile app, nor further detail on when point-of-sale or subscription-payment functionality will become available to its customers.

item_title: Nuvei and BlackLine partner on invoice-to-cash payments
item_text:
News
Payments
Nuvei and BlackLine partner on invoice-to-cash payments
Sinziana Albu
06 Aug 2026 / 5 Min Read
Nuvei has partnered with BlackLine to embed payment acceptance within BlackLine's invoice-to-cash platform for enterprise customers.
The partnership is already live with enterprise customers, according to the companies.
According to the companies, invoice-to-cash processes have become largely digital in recent years, with invoicing, accounts receivable, and financial reporting increasingly managed through dedicated finance platforms. Payment acceptance, however, has often remained separate from these workflows. This disconnect can delay collections, require manual reconciliation between payment records and open invoices, and reduce visibility into a company's cash position.
Through the process of combining BlackLine's invoice presentment and payment functionality with Nuvei's payments infrastructure, the two companies aim to close this gap. Under the partnership, customers can settle an invoice at the point of receipt, with the payment automatically matched to the corresponding receivable.
Through the integration, enterprises using BlackLine can accept cards, bank transfers, and local payment methods directly on an invoice. In addition, incoming payments are matched to open receivables without manual keying, while payment status and cash position can be tracked in real time. Payers are given a single interface through which to view, query, and settle an invoice. The companies state that funds can be collected in 150 currencies across more than 190 markets without customers needing to leave their existing finance systems.
Executive comments
Phil Fayer,
Chair and CEO of Nuvei, said the company aims for payments to function as part of the invoice-to-cash process rather than as a separate workflow, noting that finance teams expect payment functionality to operate within the systems they already use for receivables, collections, and cash flow management.
Andy Liley,
Managing Director, Invoice-to-Cash at BlackLine, said finance leaders face pressure to improve cash flow while operating more efficiently, and that payment flexibility has often been managed separately from invoicing and receivables systems.
Industry context
The partnership reflects a broader trend of payment acceptance being incorporated into finance technology stacks rather than operating as a standalone function. For Nuvei, the integration extends its payments infrastructure into platforms used by finance departments to manage liquidity, working capital, and cash flow. For BlackLine, it adds payment settlement capability to a platform historically focused on invoice presentment, accounts receivable, and financial reporting for the office of the CFO.
Neither company disclosed financial terms of the partnership or specified which enterprise customers are currently using the integration.

Garanti BBVA’dan Tapuda Güvenli ve Dijital Alım Satım
4 Ağustos 2026
Garanti BBVA’dan Tapuda Güvenli ve Dijital Alım Satım Dönemi
Garanti BBVA, Tapu ve Kadastro Genel Müdürlüğü iş birliğiyle hayata geçirilen Tapu Güvenli Alım Satım Sistemi'ni dijital kanallarına entegre etti. Sistem sayesinde gayrimenkul alım satımında ödeme ve tapu devri banka güvencesiyle eş zamanlı gerçekleşiyor. Bireysel ve kurumsal müşteriler tüm süreci Garanti BBVA Mobil ve İnternet Bankacılığı üzerinden kolayca yönetebiliyor.
Garanti BBVA, Tapu ve Kadastro Genel Müdürlüğü iş birliğiyle hayata geçirilen yeni hizmet ile birlikte, gayrimenkul alım satım işlemlerinde ödeme ve tapu devri banka güvencesi altında, eş zamanlı ve mobil ve internet bankacılığı üzerinden gerçekleştirilebiliyor.
Garanti BBVA Mobil ve İnternet Bankacılığı üzerinden kullanılabilen Tapu Güvenli Alım Satım Sistemi ile alıcı ve satıcı, işlemlerini tek bir platform üzerinden güvenle yönetebiliyor. Sistem kapsamında alıcının ödemesi, tapu devri tamamlanıncaya kadar banka güvencesiyle güvenli hesapta tutuluyor; mülkiyet devri gerçekleştiği anda ise ödeme satıcının hesabına otomatik olarak aktarılıyor.
"En önemli finansal kararlarda güveni dijital deneyimle buluşturuyoruz"
Garanti BBVA Genel Müdür Yardımcısı Cemal Onaran, yeni hizmete ilişkin değerlendirmesinde şunları söyledi: "Gayrimenkul alım satımı, müşterilerimizin hayatındaki en önemli finansal işlemlerden biri. Böylesine kritik bir süreçte güven, hız ve kolaylık büyük önem taşıyor. Tapu ve Kadastro Genel Müdürlüğü ile iş birliğimiz sayesinde ve Tapu Güvenli Alım Satım Sistemi ile, ödeme ve mülkiyet devrini banka güvencesi altında eş zamanlı gerçekleştirerek hem alıcı hem de satıcı için güvenli bir işlem ortamı sunuyoruz. Garanti BBVA Mobil ve İnternet Bankacılığı üzerinden uçtan uca dijital olarak yönetilebilen bu hizmetle müşterilerimizin süreçlerini çok daha rahat ve kontrollü şekilde tamamlayabilmelerini sağlıyoruz. Garanti BBVA olarak müşterilerimizin hayatını kolaylaştıran dijital çözümler geliştirmeye ve bankacılıkta yenilikçi uygulamalara öncülük etmeye devam edeceğiz."
Gayrimenkul alım satımında yeni bir standart
Garanti BBVA’nın bireysel ve tüzel müşterilerin kullanımına sunduğu hizmet, yüksek tutarlı gayrimenkul işlemlerinde nakit taşıma ihtiyacını ortadan kaldırırken dolandırıcılık, sahte para ve hırsızlık gibi risklerin azaltılmasına da katkı sağlıyor. Başvuru, onay ve işlem takibi tamamen dijital kanallar üzerinden gerçekleştirilebildiği için süreç daha hızlı, kontrollü ve kolay ilerliyor.

item_title: Hizmet Sektörüne Tam Destek
item_text:
Türk Ticaret Bankası Kurumsal, Ticari ve Perakendeden Sorumlu Genel Müdür Yardımcısı Ahmet Zafer Seyar, Inbusiness Dergisi tarafından düzenlenen “Hizmet İhracatında Finansmanın Önemi” başlıklı yuvarlak masa toplantısına katıldı.
Bankamızın yeni yolculuğunu, ürün ve hizmetlerini aktaran Ahmet Zafer Seyar, “Türk Ticaret Bankası olarak hizmet ve turizm sektörünü, faaliyetimizin daha ilk yıllarında olmamıza rağmen ciddi ölçüde desteklemeye başladık. Önümüzdeki dönemde de bu desteğimizi artırarak sürdüreceğiz. Geçen yılı ihracatçılarımıza sağladığımız 76,3 milyar TL’lik finansman desteğiyle tamamladık. Bu yıl hedefimiz, bu rakamı 110 milyar TL seviyesine çıkarmak. İhracatçılarımızın desteği ve sermaye yapımızın güçlenmesiyle birlikte önümüzdeki yıllarda bu finansman hacmini daha da artırmayı hedefliyoruz” diye konuştu.
Türk Ticaret Bankası’nın sektöre sağladığı desteğe değinen Seyar; “Türk Ticaret Bankası'nı diğer bankalardan ayıran en önemli özellik, ihracatçıların bankası olması. Sermayemizin %99,83'ü İhracatı Geliştirme A.Ş.'ye (İGE) ait. İGE'nin ortaklık yapısında ise Türkiye İhracatçılar Meclisi (TİM) ve 61 İhracatçı Birliği çoğunluk payına sahip. Kalan ortaklık yapısı Eximbank ve ticari bankalardan oluşuyor. Bu nedenle Türk Ticaret Bankası'nı, ihracatçıların sahip olduğu banka olarak tanımlamak yanlış olmaz. Biz, bankamızı özel sektör dinamizmiyle hareket eden ancak kamusal sorumluluk taşıyan bir misyon bankası olarak konumlandırıyoruz. Misyonumuz da, yenilikçi finansal çözümlerle ihracatçının ihtiyaç duyduğu tüm bankacılık ürün ve hizmetlerini en hızlı, en güvenli ve en uygun koşullarla sunmak. Eylül 2024 itibarıyla müşteri kabulüne başladık. 1,5 yıl gibi kısa bir sürede bireysel bankacılıktan ticari ve kurumsal bankacılığa kadar tüm ürünlere sahip konvansiyonel bir yapıyı, “fijital” banka bakış açısı ile kurduk. Bugün itibarıyla 16 şubemizle hizmet veriyoruz. Diğer ticari bankalardan temel farkımız, kredi tarafında yalnızca ihracat yapan ve döviz kazandırıcı faaliyetlerden gelir elde eden firmalarla çalışıyor olmamız. İhracatçılarımıza sunduğumuz en önemli finansman araçlarından biri reeskont kredileri. Reeskont kredilerinde güçlü bir konuma sahibiz. Bu kredilerin daha fazla ihracatçıya ulaşması için yoğun şekilde çalışıyoruz. Bu yıl, Ticaret Bakanlığımızın ihracat eylem planına Eximbank ve İGE ile birlikte Türk Ticaret Bankası da dahil oldu. 2025’te 76,3 milyar TL’ye ulaşan toplam finansman desteğimizi, 2026’da 110 milyar TL’ye yükseltmeyi hedefliyoruz. Bundan sonraki dönemde ihracatçılarımız Türk Ticaret Bankası'nı yalnızca büyüyen bir banka olarak değil, ihracatın finansmanındaki en önemli çözüm ortaklarından biri olarak görecek.
Bankamız sadece ihracat yapan firmalara kredi kullandırabiliyor. Başta ihracat kredileri olmak üzere; teminat mektubu, akreditif, Eximbank teminat mektupları, TL işletme sermayesi kredileri ile orta ve uzun vadeli yatırım kredileri sunuyoruz. Teknoloji altyapımızı, Türkiye'nin her bölgesindeki ihracatçılara hızlı ve etkin hizmet verecek şekilde kurguladık. Bu yatırımlarımız devam ediyor. İGE teminatını etkin kullanıyoruz ve KOBİ’lerimizi de finansmanla buluşturmaya gayret ediyoruz. Türkiye'de ihracatın GSYH içindeki payı yaklaşık %30 seviyesindeyken, ihracat finansmanının toplam krediler içindeki payı Eximbank dahil yaklaşık %14 seviyesinde kalıyor. Bu tablo, ihracatın finansmanında hâlâ önemli bir gelişim alanı bulunduğunu gösteriyor. Finans sektörü olarak buraya odaklanmamız ve ihracat kredilerinin toplam krediler içindeki payını artırmamız gerektiği aşikâr.
Vurgulamak istediğim bir nokta daha var: bizler üzerimize düşen görevi fazlasıyla yaparken özellikle KOBİ ihracatçılarımızın da finansal okuryazarlık konusuna eğilmesi gerektiğini düşünüyorum. Bu konuyu, Türkiye genelindeki firmalarımız açısından en temel sorunlardan biri olarak değerlendiriyorum. Finansal okuryazarlık seviyesinin yükseltilmesi büyük önem taşıyor” dedi.

item_title: Dune accepts stablecoin payments via Stripe in the EU
item_text:
News
Crypto, Web3 and CBDC
Dune becomes early EU adopter of stablecoin payments via Stripe
Sinziana Albu
07 Aug 2026 / 5 Min Read
Dune has begun accepting stablecoin payments through Stripe, allowing enterprise clients to pay for its data products and APIs in stablecoins.
For enterprises that already hold stablecoins on their balance sheets, the move addresses an existing operational gap. Payments made in stablecoins bypass foreign exchange conversion and wire transfers, with transactions posting onchain and carrying a complete audit trail. According to Neetika Bansal, Head of Connect, Money Management, and Crypto at Stripe, any business using Stripe can now accept stablecoins in the same way it accepts other payment methods, without requiring additional integrations, and can do so with instant, low-cost, and global reach. Bansal cited Dune, which serves over 1.000 enterprise teams, as an example of how this functions in practice for an institutional data business.
Stablecoin data underpinning the shift
Dune operates a dataset covering stablecoin activity across USDC, USDT, EURC, and more than 200 other stablecoins, spanning 38 blockchains. A recent report produced by Dune in partnership with Visa recorded a transfer volume of approximately EUR 32.2 trillion (USD 35 trillion) and 30 million active addresses. Dune's data indicates that major institutions are already settling transactions in stablecoins at scale. The company positions its more than 1.000 enterprise clients as part of this broader shift, with the addition of stablecoin payment acceptance framed as an extension of the infrastructure it already provides to those businesses.
Mats Olsen
, CTO of Dune, said the company's data shows stablecoins are already operating at institutional scale rather than remaining an experimental payment method. In addition, Olsen also noted that Stripe's rollout of stablecoin acceptance in the EU allowed Dune to align its payment infrastructure with the rails its customers already use.
The move reflects a broader trend of payment providers extending stablecoin acceptance to enterprise clients within the EU, where regulatory frameworks such as the Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) Regulation have shaped the operating environment for stablecoin issuance and use. For data and analytics providers serving institutional clients, enabling stablecoin settlement removes a layer of currency conversion and banking intermediation that has traditionally accompanied cross-border enterprise payments.

item_title: stc pay Bahrain partners with PayPal on transfers
item_text:
News
Payments
stc pay Bahrain and PayPal launch cross-border transfer service
Sinziana Albu
07 Aug 2026 / 5 Min Read
stc pay Bahrain and PayPal have partnered to enable direct cross-border fund transfers between the two platforms.
Under the partnership, verified stc pay Bahrain customers can securely link their PayPal accounts to their stc pay wallets. Once linked, users can fund their PayPal wallets from their stc pay accounts and withdraw available PayPal balances back into stc pay. In addition, withdrawals convert automatically from USD, PayPal's settlement currency, into BHD, the currency used in stc pay wallets. The integration is aimed at shoppers, freelancers, content creators, and small and medium-sized enterprises engaged in cross-border transactions.
Strategic rationale
According to the companies, the service responds to demand among Bahrain-based users for more direct ways to manage international payments and digital earnings. Freelancers and creators receiving payments from overseas clients, as well as consumers purchasing from international e-commerce platforms, are cited as key use cases. Through the process of linking a global digital wallet such as PayPal directly to a domestic mobile wallet, the partnership reduces the number of intermediary steps typically required to move funds between local and international accounts.
Metin Zavrak
, CEO of stc pay Bahrain, said the integration formed part of the company's broader strategy to expand its financial services offering and support Bahrain's fintech sector. Furthermore,
Otto William
s, SVP, Regional Head and General Manager, Middle East and Africa, PayPal, said the partnership was intended to widen access to cross-border commerce for consumers and businesses in the country.
The partnership positions stc pay Bahrain within a wider regional trend of mobile wallet providers seeking interoperability with international payment networks, as digital commerce and remote work continue to drive demand for cross-border payment tools in the Middle East. For PayPal, the integration extends its reach into Bahrain's digital wallet ecosystem, adding a local distribution channel for its cross-border payment infrastructure.
The companies stated that the service maintains existing compliance and security standards applied to stc pay's other financial products, with account linking subject to verification requirements.

item_title: India moves to allow merchant fees on UPI payments
item_text:
News
Payments
India moves to provide its instant payments network with a business model
Sinziana Albu
10 Aug 2026 / 5 Min Read
India has introduced legislation that could allow merchant fees to return to its Unified Payments Interface (UPI), the country's government-built instant payments network.
The
bill
, introduced in India's parliament, sets out the legal groundwork for revising the country's zero-merchant-discount-rate (MDR) policy, under which merchants have not paid fees to accept UPI payments since 2020. The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), which operates UPI, continues to record rapid growth in transaction volumes, a trend that has intensified debate over how to fund the network's ongoing expansion.
Industry pressure for a new funding model
According to the
announcement
, the proposal follows years of disagreement between the finance ministry, India's central bank, and payment companies over how to sustain UPI's infrastructure costs. Banks and fintech companies have argued that keeping merchant payments free has become increasingly difficult to maintain as transaction volumes and associated costs have grown.
Amrish Rau
, chief executive of fintech company Pine Labs, said that reaching 90% penetration and expanding UPI internationally would require startups, fintech companies, and banks to fund that expansion through continued investment in IT, innovation, and cybersecurity. It was also added that allowing the industry to recover part of these investments from merchants, while keeping consumer and peer-to-peer payments free, would help place UPI on a more sustainable footing.
The legislation itself does not impose merchant fees or specify which transactions would be affected, leaving those details to be defined at a later stage.
Potential revenue impact
Market analysts see the legislation as a possible first step toward a new revenue stream for India's payments industry. In a report published on Tuesday, Jefferies estimated that introducing merchant charges on higher-value UPI transactions could generate an additional USD 525 million to USD 1.05 billion in annual revenue by fiscal year 2028, assuming a fee of 15 to 30 basis points.
Indian daily Economic Times reported last month that officials were considering limiting any merchant charges to larger merchants rather than applying them across all UPI transactions. Bernstein, in a report last week, said such an approach would preserve UPI's consumer-friendly model while creating a new revenue pool for banks and payment companies. The brokerage noted that transactions above USD 21 account for about 4% of payment volumes but nearly 70% of transaction value.
International and market implications
The legislation will be watched closely by countries where UPI already operates, including Singapore, the UAE, and France.
The outcome could be particularly relevant for companies that dominate India's digital payments market. PhonePe, owned by Walmart, and Google Pay, owned by Alphabet, together account for nearly 80% of UPI transaction volumes, according to NPCI data. How much either company ultimately benefits will depend on how any merchant fees are eventually distributed among banks, payment apps, and other participants in the ecosystem.

item_title: Yellow Card raises USD 40 million for stablecoin expansion
item_text:
News
Crypto, Web3 and CBDC
Yellow Card raises USD 40 million to expand global stablecoin rails
Sinziana Albu
10 Aug 2026 / 5 Min Read
Yellow Card has raised USD 40 million in strategic funding from SC Ventures, Sony Innovation Fund, Polychain Capital, and Blockchain Capital.
The round brings the company's total financing to over USD 120 million since its founding.
The new capital will be used to scale Global USD Accounts, Yellow Card's dollar account product for businesses, and to expand the stablecoin rails connecting it to markets worldwide. According to the company, the financing will also deepen its presence in Latin America and Asia-Pacific, regions it is expanding into beyond its established base in Africa, and extend the local payment rails and currency coverage required to operate at a larger scale.
Global USD Accounts allow businesses to hold US dollars, hold and swap stablecoins, manage treasury functions, and collect and disburse local currencies over domestic rails in more than 50 countries. Yellow Card said the accounts run on infrastructure, it has operated for several years, and that they are already used by customers, including Visa and Western Union.
Investor rationale
Alex Manson
, CEO of SC Ventures, said stablecoin adoption depends on robust infrastructure and clear real-world utility, and described Yellow Card as positioned to scale across Africa and beyond.
Sony Innovation Fund's investment was framed by the company as reflecting institutional interest in stablecoins for global payments, with Austin Noronha, Managing Director at Sony Ventures-US, noting that the funding will support Yellow Card's expansion into Latin America, the EMEA region, and Asia-Pacific. Furthermore, Noronha pointed to the company's combination of application programming interfaces, local fiat rails, and a regulatory-first approach as relevant to banks, fintechs, and enterprises considering stablecoin-based payments.
Chris Maurice
, CEO and co-founder of Yellow Card, said the investment supports infrastructure that allows businesses to move money without relying on traditional correspondent banking, and pointed to connecting banks directly to stablecoin rails as a further opportunity.
Scale and market position
Yellow Card said it has facilitated over USD 10 billion in transactions across its network to date. The company supports more than 50 currencies and holds licences, authorisations, and registrations in 22 jurisdictions across North America, Europe, and Africa. It has established partnerships with Visa, Mastercard, PayPal, and Coinbase, which it cites as part of its positioning as an infrastructure layer for global payments providers.
The round adds to a series of institutional and strategic investments in stablecoin infrastructure providers, as banks and payment companies continue to evaluate stablecoin rails as an alternative or complement to correspondent banking for cross-border money movement, particularly in emerging markets.

item_text:
News
Crypto, Web3 and CBDC
zerohash enables stablecoin prefunding for Visa Direct clients
Sinziana Albu
10 Aug 2026 / 5 Min Read
zerohash and Visa have partnered to bring stablecoin prefunding and payout capabilities to eligible Visa Direct clients.
The partnership is set to allow Visa Direct clients to prefund accounts and disburse payouts using stablecoins, with zerohash providing the underlying infrastructure. Visa Direct, the company's real-time payments platform, reaches more than 18 billion endpoints across cards, accounts, and digital wallets in over 195 countries and territories.
Building on a 2025 pilot
The announcement extends a pilot programme Visa first unveiled at
Sibos 2025
, which tested stablecoins as a funding source for Visa Direct. Under that pilot, participating banks and payment providers could prefund transactions with stablecoins instead of depositing fiat currency in advance, with Visa treating the stablecoin balances as available funds for payouts; recipients continued to receive local currency. Visa officials said existing cross-border systems remained slow and costly, and described the pilot as a way to make funding more immediate, reduce exposure to currency fluctuations, and improve predictability in treasury operations.
Platform capabilities
zerohash supplies the regulatory and technical infrastructure behind the integration, spanning dozens of blockchains and stablecoins, alongside tools for customer usability. Edward Woodford, founder and CEO of zerohash, said the company's infrastructure already supports partners across the payments and money movement stack, including Morgan Stanley, card issuer Marqeta, and payment service provider Worldpay.
In addition, Mark Nelsen, global head of product at Visa, said the company continues to invest in infrastructure that extends the reach of Visa Direct, adding that working with zerohash is intended to bring stablecoin capabilities to clients at scale in a way that remains interoperable with existing financial systems. For businesses, the integration is designed to support settlement and cross-border money movement on a 24/7 basis, while for recipients, it is intended to increase the speed of payouts and widen access to stablecoins.
Wider regulatory and strategic context
The Visa partnership adds to zerohash's broader expansion in regulated markets. In an exclusive interview
Money20/20, The Paypers
spoke with zerohash CMO Katie Perry to understand where that shift is heading and what's actually driving t
he company. Founded in 2017, the institution built a compliance-focused infrastructure business serving institutions including BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, alongside Morgan Stanley. In 2026, zerohash obtained a MiCAR authorisation and an electronic money institution licence from the Dutch central bank, extending its regulatory footprint in Europe. Other zerohash-supported use cases include instant account funding for Interactive Brokers and near real-time cross-border contractor payments for Gusto.
At the same time, the company has also pointed to growing stablecoin use in wealth management, citing data showing that 51% of high-net-worth investors aged 18 to 40 have left a financial advisor that does not offer crypto exposure.
Taken together, the developments illustrate how stablecoins are moving beyond trading and treasury pilots into core payment network infrastructure, with Visa Direct serving as one of the larger distribution points for that shift.

item_title: Square Credit Card Levels Up: Rewards Built for Small Businesses and a New Way to Pay Vendors
item_text:
Product News
Square Credit Card Levels Up: Rewards Built for Small Businesses and a New Way to Pay Vendors
Aug 11, 2026
New Bill Pay capabilities pair with an expanded, refreshed Square Credit Card to give more sellers a simpler way to manage every outflow from one platform
DISTRIBUTED-WORKFORCE/OAKLAND, Calif – August 11, 2026 –
Square today announced a significant expansion of its Square Credit Card program and a new Square Bill Pay capability that enables sellers to fund vendor payments with their Square Credit Card, regardless of whether the vendor accepts cards. Together, the updates give sellers a more powerful way to manage cash flow, business expenses, and vendor payments from a single platform.
Operating on the American Express network, the refreshed Square Credit Card now features unlimited 3% cash back on Square Bill Pay transactions and 1.5% cash back on all other purchases. Rewards are redeemable as cash deposits into a seller’s Square Savings account, statement credit, or free processing. And now, Square Credit Card sellers can also use their card to pay more types of vendors, including those that don’t accept card payments, giving sellers more control over their cash flow.
The new features build on the card’s existing benefits: a dynamic credit line that can increase as a seller’s business grows, along with no personal guarantee, no annual fees, no late fees, and no foreign transaction fees. Additionally, the company meaningfully broadened its Bill Pay functionality, expanding it from a feature previously limited to Square Checking sellers into a more powerful accounts payable solution that all sellers can use to pay expenses.
Easing the Cash Flow Burden
For small businesses, managing outflows is just as critical as generating revenue. Across the country, half of small businesses
cite uneven cash flow
as a top financial challenge – a problem that can be exacerbated by timing mismatches between when bills are due and when sellers collect on receivables. By enabling sellers to pay vendors with their Square Credit Card regardless of the vendor’s payment method preference, Square is giving businesses more flexibility in managing cash flow while helping them earn rewards and reduce the manual overhead of managing multiple payment methods across various vendors and platforms.
“When it comes to running a trading card shop, inventory is everything. We manage over 10,000 items, and when the right cards come up, I have to move quickly. That can mean spending thousands on the spot before the window to act closes,” said Melvin Bontrager, owner of Lafayette, Indiana-based Rainer’s TCG Shop. “Square Credit Card makes that possible: I can put inventory on the card, earn cash back with every purchase, and automatically pay down my balance from my daily sales without disrupting my cash flow. And having my sales, banking, and credit card all in Square means I always know where I stand financially. When you’re moving this much inventory, that clarity is worth a lot.”
Built for Small Businesses
Most business credit cards are built to rack up airline miles and hotel points, rewards designed for frequent travelers – not for the local restaurants, salons, and shops that shape neighborhoods. Square Credit Card puts money back where it’s actually useful: unlimited 3% cash back on Square Bill Pay transactions and 1.5% cash back on every other purchase, redeemable as a cash deposit into a Square Savings account
that now earns up to 3.50% APY
, a statement credit, or free payment processing that directly reduces the cost of doing business. Since expanding eligibility at the end of last year, the number of sellers actively using Square Credit Card has doubled¹.
That seller-centric design extends to how Square has enhanced Bill Pay. Now, sellers can use their Square Credit Card to pay an even broader variety of vendors through Bill Pay, including rent, insurance, marketing expenses, and more – even when those vendors don’t accept cards. Square routes the money the way the vendor prefers to receive it, either as a direct deposit into their bank account (ACH) or a check in the mail. With 3% cash back on every Bill Pay transaction, a seller’s Square Credit Card rewards always cover the fee. Additional Bill Pay improvements include faster bill capture via OCR scanning, simplified vendor setup, and new access points across the Dashboard – supporting sellers beyond those with a Square Checking account, with external bank account funding coming soon.
“Small business owners are too often forced to choose between paying vendors on time and holding onto their cash,” said Andrea Raj, Head of Product for Square Banking. “Standalone solutions typically come with additional costs to bridge that gap, and even then, don’t solve the entire problem: you’re still spending your cash on hand, or putting it on a card not designed for small businesses. We built the opposite. Pay vendors on time, keep cash longer, and earn the right rewards for it, all in one place and while saving on fees. That’s only possible because it’s built into the platform sellers already run their business on.”
Expanding access at every level
These updates continue a year of significant investment in broadening access to Square’s financial products. Earlier this year, Square
expanded eligibility
for Square Loans through improved underwriting models that can now more accurately evaluate the creditworthiness of sellers new to the platform and seasonal operators. Square also recently partnered with Homegrown to offer
expansion capital
of up to $1 million for eligible multi-location sellers ready to open their next location. Today’s Credit Card and Bill Pay expansions extend that same commitment: more sellers can now access the credit and payment tools they need to manage cash flow on their own terms.
To learn more about Square Credit Card and Bill Pay, visit
squareup.com/banking
About Square
Square helps businesses turn transactions into connections and businesses into neighborhood favorites.
In 2009, Square started with a simple invention — the first mobile card reader, which changed how the entire financial system thinks about small businesses. Square has since grown into a global business platform helping millions of sellers of all sizes participate and thrive in their communities.
Whether independently run or a global chain, Square understands that sellers succeed when they have the freedom to focus on the experiences that keep customers coming back. From point of sale and payments to online commerce, staff management, cash flow tools, and more, Square brings together the tools sellers need to run and grow on one intelligent platform. SeerBit integrates PayPal for African merchant payments

SeerBit has integrated PayPal, enabling merchants across its supported African markets to accept payments from PayPal users at checkout.
The integration adds PayPal as a payment method alongside the cards, bank transfers, and mobile money options already supported by SeerBit, giving merchants a single system through which to manage transactions across multiple payment types.
According to the companies, the integration is intended to give merchants operating on SeerBit-powered platforms the ability to receive international payments and reach customers outside their domestic markets. SeerBit has positioned the move as a response to fragmented checkout experiences and limited payment options that have previously constrained African merchants seeking to serve international buyers. In addition, through the process of adding PayPal as a supported method, the company said merchants can offer a payment option already familiar to a large base of international shoppers, which may support buyer confidence during checkout.
The announcement frames the integration within the broader context of digital trade growth across Africa, citing increased internet adoption and expanding ecommerce activity as factors driving demand for interoperable payment infrastructure. SeerBit also linked the development to preparations for deeper regional trade integration under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), noting that accessible payment infrastructure is expected to play a role in enabling African businesses to participate in cross-border commerce.
Omoniyi Kolade
, CEO of SeerBit
, said the integration is intended to help merchants build credibility with international customers by giving them access to a payment method already trusted in global markets. Moreover,
Amir Valliani
, Vice President, Global Markets, PayPal,
described Africa as a growing region for digital commerce, pointing to rising connectivity and an increasing number of digitally native businesses, and said the integration is designed to help SeerBit's merchants reach more international customers and build trust with them.
Market context
The integration adds to a broader trend of global payment providers extending their reach into African markets through partnerships with local payment infrastructure companies, rather than direct market entry. For SeerBit, the PayPal integration extends the range of payment methods available through its existing platform, which already supports card payments, bank transfers, and mobile money across the markets it operates in.
The move reflects continued interest from international payment providers in facilitating cross-border e-commerce on the continent, an area where inconsistent payment infrastructure has historically been cited as a barrier to merchants seeking to sell beyond their home markets.

item_text:
News
Payments
AFC urges Oregon to revise proposed BNPL licensing rules
Paula Albu
11 Aug 2026 / 5 Min Read
The American Fintech Council (AFC) has submitted a comment letter to the Oregon Department of Consumer and Business Services (DCBS), Division of Financial Regulation, urging the agency to reconsider its proposed bulletin regarding consumer finance and payday licensing requirements for buy now, pay later (BNPL) products.
AFC's core concerns
AFC has called on the Division to adopt a more tailored regulatory approach reflecting what it describes as the distinct structure and consumer protections associated with responsible BNPL products. The organisation has urged the Division to reconsider applying Oregon's existing payday lending and consumer finance licensing framework to BNPL products, arguing that regulations designed for high-cost payday lending may not reflect the structure of BNPL products and could introduce regulatory uncertainty for providers.
AFC has also asked the Division to clarify that merchant compensation arrangements should be treated separately from consumer finance charges, arguing that these fees compensate BNPL providers for payment-related services rather than representing a charge associated with extending credit to consumers.
Position on the purchase money loan exclusion and rulemaking process
AFC has asked the Division to reconsider its interpretation of the purchase money loan exclusion, arguing that BNPL products are designed to finance specific retail purchases at the point of sale and should be assessed based on their transaction-specific structure rather than whether they are secured by collateral.
The organisation has also recommended that any significant changes to BNPL regulation in Oregon be pursued through a formal rulemaking process. AFC described the proposed bulletin as representing a substantial expansion of existing regulatory expectations and recommended that the Division adopt a transparent, stakeholder-driven process for developing any future regulatory framework.
Company commentary
A company official at AFC said responsible BNPL providers offer consumers an alternative to traditional forms of credit, citing clear repayment terms and predictable schedules as features distinguishing these products, and said Oregon policymakers have an opportunity to establish a regulatory approach that allows consumers to continue accessing these products.
A separate company official at AFC said Oregon's approach to regulating BNPL products should be informed by a review of existing statutes, recognition of the specific structure of BNPL products, and engagement with industry stakeholders before new compliance requirements are introduced.
Broader context
AFC represents more than 150 member companies and partners across the fintech and banking sectors and describes itself as promoting responsible innovation and sound public policy within financial services. The letter reflects a broader ongoing debate among US states regarding how existing consumer credit and payday lending frameworks should apply to BNPL products, as regulators continue to assess how these products should be classified and supervised relative to traditional forms of consumer credit.

item_title: Rain acquires merchant wallet startup Ansa
item_text:
News
M&A and Investments
Stablecoin card issuer Rain acquires merchant wallet startup Ansa
Sinziana Albu
12 Aug 2026 / 5 Min Read
Rain has acquired Ansa, a merchant wallet startup, to combine prefunded balances with its stablecoin card issuing platform.
The transaction adds a fiat-based product to Rain's platform: Ansa's wallets hold dollar balances that customers load in advance and spend at the issuing brand. Neither company described a stablecoin component in the acquired technology. According to the announcement, Rain intends to combine these prefunded balances with its existing Visa and Mastercard issuing capability, allowing a balance to be spent outside the merchant that originally issued it, and to operate wallets, rewards, and stablecoins from a single platform.
Merchant wallet infrastructure
Ansa offered its wallet infrastructure through white-label APIs and mobile SDKs, alongside an incentive engine that attaches expiration dates to rewards to encourage repeat visits. Its client base has included Compass Coffee, a coffee chain based in Washington, D.C., and Reverb, a music gear marketplace. According to a case study published by Ansa, Compass Coffee recorded a 30% increase in visits among customers who adopted the wallet. Rain co-founder and chief executive Farooq Malik announced the acquisition on X, stating that the combined product would target sectors including sports teams, venues, hotels, and cruise lines.
Rain has said that Ansa established an arrangement with Mastercard allowing a closed-loop balance to be spent in-store over Mastercard's rails at existing terminals, while online and in-app transactions would authorise through Ansa's API rather than a card network. Neither Mastercard nor Ansa has published details of this arrangement. Ansa's own release announcing its in-store product, Ansa Anywhere, in September 2024, described the offering as tap-to-pay functionality through Apple Pay and Google Pay, and as compatible with any POS or payment service provider, without reference to Mastercard.
Second acquisition in nine months
The Ansa deal is Rain's second acquisition within nine months. In November 2025, the company acquired Uptop, a card-linked rewards platform that runs fan programmes for the Cleveland Cavaliers, the Detroit Pistons, and LSU athletics. That acquisition followed a 58 million USD Series B round led by Sapphire Ventures. On 9 January 2026, Rain raised 250 million USD in a Series C round led by ICONIQ at a valuation of 1.95 billion USD, taking total funding above 338 million USD.
Following this initiative, Rain has linked the Ansa acquisition to its agentic commerce strategy, describing a stored value balance governed by rules on spending scope, location, and duration as comparable to the scoped cards it offers for AI agents. Goldberg is expected to contribute to this product, though Rain has not specified a timeline.

item_text:

Fintech
SIDBI deploys MonetaGo's Secure Financing for MSME loans
Paula Albu
12 Aug 2026 / 5 Min Read
SIDBI (Small Industries Development Bank of India) and MonetaGo have announced the go-live of MonetaGo's Secure Financing system on SIDBI's GST-Sahay Invoice Based Financing Platform, following completion of a pilot programme.
Extending invoice validation across factoring platforms
The deployment allows SIDBI to validate invoices financed through the Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS), while also enabling invoice validation across other participating factoring platforms and lenders, including SBI Global Factors and India Factoring. SIDBI said the deployment reflects its continued focus on strengthening secure, transparent, and optimal financing infrastructure for micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in India.
Timeline of the deployment
The go-live follows SIDBI's announcement in November 2025 that it would adopt MonetaGo's Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) technology. Following a pilot phase and three months of live production beginning in March 2026, Secure Financing has now been deployed across SIDBI's GST-Sahay lending operations for invoice-based financing.
SIDBI operates as India's principal development financial institution focused on the promotion, financing, and development of MSMEs, supporting financial inclusion and MSME participation in domestic and global value chains through its lending and development initiatives.
Company commentary
A company official at SIDBI described the implementation of Secure Financing as an important step in the institution's efforts to build a trusted and efficient MSME lending ecosystem, noting that the platform has strengthened confidence across SIDBI's GST-Sahay financing workflows and is intended to support faster, more informed lending decisions for both borrowers and financiers.
A company official at MonetaGo said SIDBI's deployment demonstrates that Digital Public Infrastructure can be implemented at scale within institutional lending environments, describing the deployment as reflecting the maturity of interoperable, standards-based infrastructure within India's financing ecosystem. A separate company official at MonetaGo said the deployment illustrates how DPI can strengthen institutional lending and support broader access to MSME finance following a period of stable production.
Broader context for MonetaGo's platform in India
MonetaGo's Secure Financing system has formed part of India's digital trade finance infrastructure since 2018. According to MonetaGo, the number of MSMEs receiving financing through Reserve Bank of India-supported platforms underpinned by its technology has increased by 319% since the start of 2023, which the company said reflects the broader impact of secure, interoperable infrastructure on access to MSME credit.
MonetaGo describes Secure Financing as a trade finance registry designed to prevent fraud related to invoices and other trade documents. According to the company, its solutions have been in production since 2018 and are used to prevent losses across the trade finance sector, with MonetaGo noting it was the first third-party service integrated into Swift's API-enabled infrastructure.

item_title: MoonPay Enterprise: new stablecoin payments platform
item_text:
News
Crypto, Web3 and CBDC
MoonPay launches MoonPay Enterprise stablecoin platform
Sinziana Albu
12 Aug 2026 / 5 Min Read
MoonPay has launched MoonPay Enterprise, a stablecoin payments platform built on Iron, the infrastructure provider it acquired in 2025.
The platform is described as the company's largest expansion since it acquired Iron, an API-first stablecoin infrastructure provider, in March 2025.
Addressing fragmented infrastructure
According to the company, businesses building stablecoin-based payment flows previously had to combine multiple providers to cover fiat on-ramps, stablecoin issuance, and cross-border settlement separately. This fragmented approach added vendor dependencies, cost, and compliance overhead for companies operating across jurisdictions.
MoonPay Enterprise is designed to consolidate these functions into a single platform. It uses Iron's technology to let companies issue virtual accounts, manage treasuries in multiple currencies, and transfer funds through established rails such as ACH, wire transfer, and SWIFT. Incoming fiat is converted into stablecoins and settled into wallets through one API, according to the company.
MoonPay Enterprise is structured around four core functions. Pay In allows businesses to collect fiat through local payment rails, including SEPA, ACH, FPS, and PIX, as well as SWIFT, with funds received into virtual accounts and automatically converted into stablecoins. Convert provides access to institutional stablecoin liquidity for treasury management and large over-the-counter conversions. At the same time, Pay Out enables global payouts settled either in stablecoins or local fiat currencies across supported markets. Issue allows businesses to mint fully reserved, white-label stablecoins using built-in issuance infrastructure.
A company representative said the platform is intended to let businesses access issuance, conversion, and settlement capabilities through a single integration, without needing to build in-house expertise in banking infrastructure or blockchain operations.
MoonPay Enterprise operates on top of MoonPay's existing regulatory coverage, which includes money transmitter licences in all 50 US states, a New York BitLicense, MiCA approval in the EU, and registrations in the UK, Canada, Australia, and other markets. The platform holds SOC 2, PCI DSS, and ISO 27001 certifications. MoonPay stated that it already processes hundreds of millions in volume across more than 190 countries for more than 50 enterprise partners.
Early adopters
MoonPay Enterprise is live and already in use by several partners. Deel is using the platform to support stablecoin payroll, while Paysafe has integrated it within a payments platform that processes an annual volume of USD 167 billion, enabling merchants to accept cryptocurrency at checkout. Other named partners include Whop, WalletConnect, Ingenico, Avici, Exodus, Citrea, and Scopex.
Furthermore, the launch reflects a broader trend of payments providers building consolidated infrastructure layers for stablecoin adoption, as businesses increasingly look to combine treasury management, cross-border settlement, and payroll functions with fewer intermediaries. Regulatory clarity in markets such as the EU under MiCA, alongside existing US state-level licensing frameworks, is likely to remain a factor shaping how such platforms expand across jurisdictions.

item_title: EU to review MiCA stablecoin rules for non-EU issuers
item_text:
News
Crypto, Web3 and CBDC
EU to review MiCA framework for non-EU stablecoin issuers
Sinziana Albu
12 Aug 2026 / 5 Min Read
The EU has started reviewing its MiCA framework to address licensing barriers facing non-EU stablecoin issuers such as Tether and Circle.
The European Commission's Directorate-General for Financial Stability, Financial Services and Capital Markets Union is consulting on potential changes to the stablecoin provisions, according to a report by ChainCatcher.
Under the existing MiCA rules, major foreign stablecoin issuers, including Tether, have been unable to secure authorisation to operate in the EU market. According to a Circle official, this situation leaves European crypto users without adequate protection and limits their access to widely used stablecoins. Furthermore, the review is reportedly influenced by developments in the US, where the GENIUS Act has established a federal framework for stablecoin issuance, and where the current administration has prioritised stablecoin policy.
MiCA's transition period and scope
MiCA was approved by the Council of the EU on 16 May 2023, based on market conditions that predate more recent developments in the stablecoin sector by over three years. The transition period allowing crypto-asset service providers to operate under national licensing regimes ended on 1 July 2026, marking full application of the framework across the bloc. EU diplomats are also assessing whether to expand MiCA's scope to cover tokenised payment methods and tokenised deposits, areas not addressed under the current regulation.
Implications for the stablecoin market
According to the
announcement
, any adjustment to MiCA's stablecoin provisions could affect how non-EU issuers approach the European market, potentially opening a path to authorisation for issuers such as Tether. At the same time, it could also influence the competitive position of EU-authorised stablecoin issuers, including Circle, which has already obtained authorisation under the existing framework. The outcome of the review may shape how the EU aligns its regulatory approach with international developments, including the US GENIUS Act, as global stablecoin regulation continues to evolve alongside the growing use of tokenised payment instruments.

item_title: Flywire expands Trustly partnership in US, Canada
item_text:
News
Payments
Flywire expands Trustly partnership in US, Canada
Sinziana Albu
12 Aug 2026 / 5 Min Read
Flywire has expanded its partnership with Trustly to bring Open Banking payments to payers in the US and Canada.
According to the official press release, in the US, this will operate via ACH transfers, while in Canada it will use Pre-Authorised Debit (PAD). The move builds on a partnership between the two companies that began in Europe in 2017, before expanding into other markets over time.
Under the arrangement, payers authorise transactions by logging into their existing online bank accounts through Trustly's interface, rather than manually entering routing and account numbers. In addition, Flywire said this method is intended to reduce payment failures and give payers visibility into the status of their transactions throughout the process.
According to Flywire, Trustly carries out a balance check at the point of authorisation, designed to flag potential insufficient funds before a transaction is processed, which the companies said reduces the risk of non-sufficient funds (NSF) returns. For cross-border payments, Flywire said it manages funds during the post-settlement return window, which it described as lowering the likelihood of reversals and providing more predictable outcomes for clients.
Flywire also said payers are shown processing timelines and pricing information within its payment interface before authorising a transaction, with no additional wire fees or bank charges cited in the announcement.
Regulatory context across markets
Flywire said the expansion reflects its capacity to manage differing Open Banking regulatory and technical frameworks across the US, Canada, and Europe.
Kate Moran
, Vice President of Global Payments at Flywire, said the company is applying Open Banking infrastructure it has developed in Europe to the North American market, with the aim of offering clients a payment method already established elsewhere.
A Trustly executive said the expanded partnership is intended to extend Open Banking to sectors involving higher-value payments, combining bank-login-based authorisation with underlying risk-mitigation processes designed for enterprise clients.
Flywire provides payment and software services across sectors, including education, healthcare, and travel, enabling domestic and cross-border transactions for its client base. Trustly provides Open Banking-based account-to-account payment services. The expanded offering is aimed at both domestic and cross-border payments made by US and Canadian payers to Flywire's clients.

item_title: NAPAS, BIDV, Weixin Pay expand QR payments
item_text:
News
Payments
NAPAS, BIDV, Weixin Pay expand cross-border QR payments
Paula Albu
12 Aug 2026 / 5 Min Read
The National Payment Corporation of Vietnam (NAPAS), the Bank for Investment and Development of Vietnam (BIDV), and Weixin Pay have announced an expansion of cross-border QR payment services between Vietnam and China, extending digital payment connectivity between the two countries.
Completing NAPAS' connection with Weixin Pay
The partnership completes NAPAS' QR payment connection with Weixin Pay, allowing Chinese visitors to pay by scanning VietQRGlobal codes at outlets across Vietnam. According to NAPAS, the service is expected to reach more than 1 billion Weixin Pay users in China. Weixin Pay, also known as WeChat Pay, is among the more widely used mobile payment platforms in China, supporting both online and in-store payments across multiple sectors.
How the service works
Under the arrangement, Chinese travellers can use the Weixin app to scan VietQRGlobal codes at retail stores, restaurants, hotels, accommodation providers, and tourist attractions across Vietnam. Transactions are processed through payment infrastructure jointly operated by NAPAS and Weixin Pay, with BIDV serving as the settlement bank.
According to NAPAS, Weixin Pay is the third Chinese payment platform to complete cross-border QR payment integration with its network, following earlier integrations with other Chinese payment providers.
Company commentary
A company official at NAPAS said the connection completes QR payment interoperability for Chinese visitors in Vietnam while extending VietQRGlobal's reach to one of the larger payment user markets globally, adding that the cooperation is expected to improve the customer experience and support economic ties between the two countries as cross-border payment demand continues to grow alongside tourism and trade.
Additionally, a company official at BIDV said the expanded service is intended to provide a more convenient payment option for travellers while helping connect the two economies through digital financial infrastructure, adding that the bank will continue working with the government, the State Bank of Vietnam, and other partners to support cashless payments, businesses, tourism, and trade.
A company official at Weixin Pay said the initiative is intended to improve the travel experience for Chinese visitors, encourage spending, and help Vietnamese businesses better serve international customers.
Planned next phase
NAPAS said the three partners are studying a further phase of the project that would allow Vietnamese travellers to use domestic banking apps and e-wallets to scan QR codes and make payments while in China, to create a more integrated cross-border payment structure to support tourism, trade, and broader economic exchange between the two countries.

item_title: Commerce now moves at the speed of culture. And anyone can move with it.
item_text:
Skip to Content
by Shopify Data Science
Share this story
Read more
The preparedness paradox: Wait for “ready,” and it might never come
The data says founders would do it again. Even in this economy.
Entrepreneurship has no zip code
Entrepreneurs turn culture's biggest moments into something you can hold. New data shows how fast they do it, and how it shapes the way we live and connect.
The distance between a cultural moment and a business built on it used to be measured in weeks or months. Now it's hours. Sometimes even minutes.
Starting a business and reaching that first sale has never been faster or more open to more people. It means a seller can respond to a cultural moment almost as it happens. And that becomes the enabling condition for everything else.
In 2025, nearly 10% of new shops made their first sale within a single day of signing up, an increase of 43% in just three years. Half of all new sellers now reach their first sale within about three weeks.
On May 8, 2025, white smoke rose over the Sistine Chapel and the world learned the name of the new pope. Within an hour, you could buy a T-shirt emblazoned with "da pope."
One of the shops selling Pope Leo gear was
Obvious Shirts
, run by Joe Johnson, a Chicago entrepreneur who'd started years earlier making one-liner shirts for Cubs fans. He didn't have a manufacturing deal or a warehouse full of inventory waiting on a papal conclave. He had an idea, a storefront, and the instinct to move fast.
For most of retail history, turning a moment into a product meant already having capital, inventory, manufacturing relationships, and shelf space. The moment would pass long before an ordinary person could act on it. Today, commerce can move at the speed of culture.
Entrepreneurs are now the fastest translators between culture and the economy, taking the moments we witness and turning them into something we can hold. And you no longer have to already be in business to do it.
When the time from idea to income narrows, high-agency people can act on an idea fast, whether they're starting something new or already running a shop. As those barriers keep falling, less and less stands between spotting a moment and selling into it.
Moving at the speed of the moment
A century ago, sociologist Émile Durkheim studied why people gather for rituals and named the energy that builds when a crowd experiences something together:
collective effervescence
. He noticed that the feeling needs somewhere to live once everyone goes home, so it attaches itself to an object, a totem, that lets people carry the belonging with them.
A championship tee or a World Cup scarf is a totem in that sense. Commerce is how an experience gets a physical form. It takes a moment you'd otherwise just watch on a screen and makes it something you can touch, wear, and stand inside of. That's the difference between witnessing a moment and belonging to it. And why merch is so enduring.
Sports are the purest test of speed, because there's a shared, public time stamp. Everyone knows the exact minute the final whistle, the buzzer-beater, or the trophy lift happened, so it’s easy to see how quickly commerce catches up.
During the New York Knicks' 2026 playoff run, more than 3,000 shops listed orange-and-blue products, and the typical one made its first sale within three days.
Then there's the World Cup, which wrapped in July and created breakout moments faster than anyone could plan for. When an underdog became the tournament's improbable hero, people around the world reached for a way to celebrate him. Sellers kept pace, half of them making a first sale within three days, this time for fans spread across continents.
And then a certain soccer player wandered into
Wild Bill's Western Store
, a family-run shop in downtown Dallas, and walked out with a taxidermied raccoon clutching a whiskey bottle. The image went viral, and since that June visit Wild Bill's online sales rose 10x compared to a month earlier. The owners switched on global shipping for the first time.
When a trend becomes a category
The same low barriers that let someone catch a one-week wave also build lasting categories.
Take matcha. It didn't explode overnight. It was a wellness habit, then an aesthetic, then a genuine staple. A wave of independent brands launched or expanded alongside it, from
Morning Made
in Australia to
Matcha Mystic
in the Netherlands.
When the craze peaked in 2025, nearly 1,500 new shops launched to meet it. The easy assumption is that they would disappear when the hype cooled. Instead the majority of them (70%) are still active today, with most reaching their first sale within about two weeks of listing a product. What started as a trend is becoming a category, with sales continuing to climb quarter over quarter.
protein
changed from a bodybuilder's obsession to a number that all shoppers scan for on the back of a package, entrepreneurs met the moment. Over the past year, protein coffee sales climbed 507% and prepared protein foods 194%, while traditional protein shakes fell 40%. Sellers moved in to meet this shift in demand, with 76% more shops selling protein coffee and 37% more selling prepared protein foods year over year, each with its own idea of what a protein product can be, from ramen to cereal.
Both of these were dismissed as passing trends until, at some point no one can quite name, they became the default.
The barriers are collapsing
The time it takes to reach that first sale keeps shrinking, and that helps entrepreneurs whether they're building for a moment or building for a decade. The sooner someone makes a sale, the sooner they know the idea works.
Now the distance between what culture wants and what an entrepreneur can deliver has disappeared.

item_title: Defacto taps Mambu Payments for embedded SME financing
item_text:
News
Fintech
Defacto and Mambu launch embedded SME financing in France
Sinziana Albu
13 Aug 2026 / 5 Min Read
Defacto has gone live on Mambu Payments with SEPA connectivity to support the payment flows of its receivable financing product for a France-based financial institution.
The deployment supports Defacto's work with an institutional banking partner described as one of France's financial institutions, and is designed to meet the operational and regulatory requirements associated with that relationship.
Technical approach and integration
Rather than building and maintaining direct bank integrations internally, Defacto has connected to SEPA payment rails through Mambu Payments via a REST API. The company has stated that this gives it real-time visibility across payment flows, alongside a reusable architecture that is currently being extended to a second institutional partner.
In addition, an important feature of the implementation is that Defacto continues to operate on top of its existing accounts held with its institutional banking partner, rather than opening new accounts with a third-party custodian bank, as is typically required under BaaS models. Instead of restructuring its banking setup, Defacto has kept its existing tier-one banking relationship in place and automated the payment operations layer above it.
Founded in 2021, Defacto has financed more than EUR 1.5 billion for over 25,000 SMEs across five European markets. The collaboration with Mambu progressed from initial product scoping in July 2025, through a beta launch in November 2025, to full production deployment in January 2026.
Jordane Giuly
, CEO & Co-Founder, Defacto, said the company's institutional banking partnerships require payments infrastructure that is secure and reliable, and that working with Mambu Payments allowed engineering resources to be directed toward customer-facing development rather than bank connectivity. According to the official, the resulting infrastructure supports Defacto's current programmes and provides scope for further partner expansion.
Moreover,
Victor Mithouard
, VP Payments & Strategy, Mambu, said that as financial institutions adopt Embedded Finance, payment infrastructure is becoming a differentiating factor for fintechs. It was also added that Defacto's deployment shows how API-based infrastructure can support faster market entry and institutional partnership scaling without bespoke bank integration projects, and that the underlying automation provides the real-time connectivity needed for Defacto to run its lending programmes within its banking partner's infrastructure.
Market context
As Embedded Finance extends further into regulated financial services, payment infrastructure has become a component of bringing new lending products to market. For providers such as Defacto, connecting to existing banking relationships through standardised APIs, rather than through new custodian arrangements, is presented as an alternative to traditional BaaS deployment. The partnership also reflects continued activity by Mambu in the European payments infrastructure space, following its established position in cloud banking technology.

item_text:
News
Payments
finby deploys Wero for pan-European ecommerce payments
Sinziana Albu
13 Aug 2026 / 5 Min Read
finby has deployed Wero, the pan-European A2A payment solution developed by the European Payments Initiative (EPI), for its ecommerce merchants.
The deployment allows finby's ecommerce merchants to accept payments made directly from consumers' bank accounts, using instant transfer infrastructure rather than card-based rails.
Wero was developed by EPI and is backed by 18 European banks and payment providers, with more than 50 financial institutions participating in the initiative overall. The solution has been built on instant A2A transfers, enabling consumers to pay directly from their bank accounts without routing transactions through card networks.
Moreover, the solution has so far been used primarily for P2P and, increasingly, in-store payments, and has now begun expanding into ecommerce payments, a segment in which finby's deployment positions the company among an early group of acquirers offering the method to online merchants.
Strategic context for finby
finby has described the Wero deployment as part of a longer-term strategy focused on local payment methods and cross-border commerce. The company said it intends to continue expanding its portfolio with payment solutions aimed at supporting merchants operating across multiple European markets.
Commenting on the deployment,
David Rintel
, CEO of finby, said the move represents a step towards a more unified European payments ecosystem, adding that the company sees Wero as combining simplicity, security, and what he described as payment sovereignty for the region. Rintel also noted that finby sees potential for the method within the evolving European ecommerce landscape.
Martina Weimert,
CEO of EPI, said finby's deployment helps expand access to Wero for both consumers and merchants, noting that the aim is to offer what she described as a competitive European payment solution with a fast and secure payment experience.
Industry implications
The integration reflects a broader trend among European payment service providers to diversify beyond card-based acceptance and incorporate instant, bank-based payment rails. A2A payment methods have gained regulatory and industry attention across the EU as alternatives to card schemes, partly in the context of discussions around European payment sovereignty and reducing dependence on non-European card networks.
For merchants, the addition of Wero alongside existing payment methods may offer an additional route to accept payments from consumers in markets where the scheme already has an established user base, particularly Belgium, France, and Germany. As Wero's ecommerce functionality continues to roll out, further deployments by acquirers and payment service providers across the region are likely to shape the pace of adoption among merchants and consumers alike.
